findings.claim: In `.topic-meta-data h5 a` the light and dark values are swapped. The original `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` instead of (30%, 70%). On the default light theme the bold poster-name link goes from dark grey to pale grey, which is a light-theme change outside the commit's dark-theme-only intent. The dark-theme value is also wrong.
findings.evidence: The diff text shows `- $lightness: 30%` paired with `+ (70%, 30%)` (`git diff 7554b5e3c4 d38c4d5f74 -- app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss`). The superpowers pairing script prints this line with orig=30 light=70 dark=30. Superpowers computed light-theme contrast against white dropping from #646464 (5.92:1) to #bdbdbd (1.88:1), which is below WCAG AA. That figure assumes the default #222/#fff palette. Nothing was compiled because no sass toolchain was available, so the effect is reasoned.
findings.reason: Accepted, Important, raised by 3 seats. Red check: the superpowers pairing script over the pinned patch, which flags this line (orig=30 light=70 dark=30). Turn it green by restoring (30%, 70%).

findings.claim: The conversion is incomplete. `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses a bare `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`, which the commit message says must use $secondary for dark themes. On dark themes this badge will differ from its neighbours.
findings.evidence: `git grep -nE 'scale-color\(\s*\$primary\s*,\s*\$lightness:\s*[0-9]' -- app/assets plugins | grep -v dark-light-choose` finds only this line plus a comment (mattpocock; ponytail confirms). Superpowers states the opposite: that no unwrapped `scale-color($primary` remains.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by 2 seats, so it is not fixed this loop. Superpowers' contrary completeness claim does not disprove it, because two seats cite a concrete grep hit. ponytail: one-line wrap at _topic-list.scss:115 when dark-theme greys are next touched.

findings.evidence: The same grep matches this comment line (mattpocock). Ponytail notes the match is a comment but does not call it stale.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by 1 seat, so it is not fixed this loop. ponytail: refresh the comment alongside any follow-up to _topic-list.scss:115.

findings.claim: The same `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, X%), scale-color($secondary, (100-X)%))` expression is copied by hand 115 times across 32 files, starting at common/admin/admin_base.scss:385. The 100-X rule is never written down, so a later edit that changes one number but not the other compiles silently. A one-argument helper next to `dark-light-choose` or `dark-light-diff` would encode the rule.
findings.evidence: Ponytail's script checked that all 115 added lines satisfy dark = 100 - light. The repo precedent is `dark-light-diff` in variables.scss and commit 54c0bea294. Mattpocock flags the same pattern as an advisory Duplicated Code smell. Open-code-review explicitly declined to flag it, so it does not count as a seat.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by 2 advisory seats only. The finding is non-blocking, and no new abstraction is added inside the fix loop. ponytail: consider a primary-faded($pct) helper beside dark-light-choose in a follow-up.

findings.claim: The patch adds a stray space before `}` in single-line rules (`...)); }`), here and in desktop/topic-list.scss:39-54 and several desktop/topic-post.scss one-liners. This does not match the surrounding style.
findings.evidence: Superpowers raised this from reading the diff, with no command. Mattpocock's report states that the `{color: ...;}` brace spacing in these single-line rules already existed at base and was not introduced by the patch, and that no trailing whitespace was added.
findings.reason: Disproved by a seat report: mattpocock states this single-line brace spacing pre-exists at base 7554b5e3c4, so the patch did not introduce it. The finding is Minor, so no verifier is needed.

coverage: Files skipped: none. All four seats report reviewing all 32 patched files. Mattpocock and ponytail checked most files by script and read context manually only at the flagged sites. Open-code-review worked from a partial clone, so it took base values from the patch's - lines rather than base blobs. Axes that did not run: (1) The gate did not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored by executed checks. (2) There is no spec; every seat judged against the commit message 'scale-color $lightness must use $secondary for dark themes'. (3) No sass compiler was available, so there is no compiled-CSS or rendered check. Every main-list colour effect and the superpowers contrast figures are reasoned from the diff and from scale-color semantics, assuming the default #222/#fff palette. The repo has no SCSS tests. (4) Standards docs are limited to CONTRIBUTING.md; there is no scss-lint config and no CODING_STANDARDS file. (5) Nobody checked visually whether the 100-X dark-theme mirror looks right per rule. (6) Superpowers' claim that no unwrapped scale-color($primary remains is contradicted by the grep from mattpocock and ponytail (see _topic-list.scss:115). (7) No fix rounds or scoped re-reviews ran, so nothing has converged; all five main-list Important findings remain open.
